transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Evelyn Park, Marcus Liu, Priya Nair (Redwood); Daniel Reyes, Asha Kapoor, Tom Bennett, Lina Morales (Novus Dynamics)

[00:00] Evelyn (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — say your name and role and then we'll jump in.
[00:18] Daniel (Novus CTO): Daniel Reyes, CTO at Novus. Thanks, Evelyn.
[00:22] Asha (Novus): Asha Kapoor, ML Platform. We'll be focused on migration feasibility.
[00:27] Tom (Novus): Tom Bennett, DevOps. I'll be evaluating infra implications.
[00:31] Lina (Novus): Lina Morales, Security. I'll watch for compliance bits.
[00:34] Evelyn: Great. Marcus and Priya from my side — Marcus will run the technical demo and Priya will show a couple of Optimize suggestions.
[00:42] Marcus (Redwood SE): Hi all. Quick agenda: parity mapping for endpoints, streaming & function-calling quirks, performance & cost tradeoffs, then private deployment and security. We'll leave 15 minutes for questions and next steps.
[01:05] Daniel: High level — we're running a mix of OpenAI chat completions and some Anthropic Claude endpoints plus a handful of Together models in prod. We need parity: same responses or acceptable deltas, same latency characteristics, and cost improvements ideally.
[01:20] Marcus: Perfect. First thing — call shape. OpenAI-style chat with function-calling maps straightforwardly to Redwood's chat/generation endpoints. We do have a couple of gotchas — tokenization differences and streaming chunk boundaries can change mid-response which affects cutoffs.
[01:40] Asha: When you say tokenization differences — can you quantify impact? We have prompt sets with long system messages sometimes 1.5k tokens.
[01:48] Marcus: Yeah so, redwood uses a similar tokenizer to the open models we surface but there are small differences; in practice we saw 1-4% token delta across our benchmarks — depends on newlines and whitespace. For your long system messages it's worth running the parity tool. We'll include tokenized counts in the parity-sheet.
[02:10] Tom: On performance — we care about p95 latency under load. We're doing 40 rps with bursts to 200 for certain customers.
[02:18] Marcus: Understood. With Dedicated or Private pools you can pin capacity. For hosted we recommend autoscale + burst but that has slight cold start variance. Our benchmarks: on equivalent GPU families, p95 within 10-15% of what teams see on OpenAI when using similar batching. We'll share trace examples.
[02:40] Daniel: Can you explain batching — our app is latency-sensitive so we avoid batching in some flows.
[02:46] Priya (Redwood Product): Sure — Redwood Optimize can recommend per-route batching windows. If a route is low-latency critical we keep batch size 1 and enable KV-prefix caching so repeated context doesn't re-run. For bulk workflows we expand batching for cost gains.
[03:05] [crosstalk] Asha: KV what?
[03:08] Marcus: KV cache — think of the key/value cache for decoder states, we sometimes see it transcribed as KV cash in notes, sorry. It avoids recomputing prefixes for interactive sessions which cuts token compute by up to 30% on long chats.
[03:27] Lina: Security — what about data at rest, KMS, and audit logs? We need AES-256 at rest and customer-managed keys.
[03:34] Evelyn: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations and you can bring your own key via our KMS bridge. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available in the console. We'll attach the SOC2 pack.
[03:47] Lina: Also need RBAC and SSO.
[03:50] Evelyn: SSO/SAML is supported; we also have fine-grained API keys and token scoping in the console.
[04:01] Marcus: Back to parity — the main mapping is: OpenAI chat.create -> Redwood /v1/chat endpoint; messages map 1:1. Anthropic completions with their safety layers map to our filtered codecs; Together API tends to be model-variant specific so we recommend a tiny shim for any custom parameters. We can supply a mapping script.
[04:28] Daniel: Can latency-sensitive flows use streaming? Any differences in chunk timing?
[04:33] Marcus: Yes streaming is supported. Difference to watch: chunk sizes and flushing frequency can vary; some client-side stream parsers expect token-level flushes — Redwood streams at token and sub-token boundaries; sometimes the transcription writes subtoken as part of previous token — you'll see slight differences. Client SDKs handle that.
[04:55] Asha: Function calling — we rely heavily on auto-extracting structured outputs. Does Redwood support the same spec?
[05:02] Marcus: We support function-like outputs and structured schema enforcement. Our function-calling is compatible with the common OpenAI-style approach, but we recommend adding a thin adapter to handle edge-case JSON parse differences. We'll include a sample adapter in the parity repo.
[05:20] Tom: For private vs hosted — what's the network topology for Private? VPC peering or private link?
[05:25] Evelyn: Private offers both VPC approaches: VPC peering or an AWS PrivateLink-style connector depending on your infra. For on-prem we provide a package and secure control plane with outbound-only control channel optional.
[05:40] Lina: Data residency — we need all inference logs retained in-region for EU customers.
[05:45] Priya: You can choose region pinning and set log retention policies per dataset in the console. We'll work with you on retention windows.
[05:55] Marcus: Now I'll share my screen and walk through a short parity demo.
[06:10] [screen share start] Marcus: Opening the parity workbook — this has three columns: source endpoint (OpenAI/Anthropic/Together), Redwood endpoint mapping, and token delta/cost delta. For example, an OpenAI gpt-x call with function-calling maps to Redwood-chat.v1 with function schema. The parity sheet link is in the notes: https://redwood.example/parity/novus (note: we'll push a sanitized copy to your workspace).
[06:48] Daniel: You mentioned cost delta — can you show a rough example?
[06:52] Marcus: Sure. For a sample prompt set we ran yesterday: OpenAI baseline cost $0.018 per 1k tokens (example), Redwood served on equivalent model costs $0.009–0.012 per 1k tokens depending on quantization/reporting. With quantized variants you trade = slight quality delta but cost down 25–40%.
[07:18] Asha: Quantization concerns — do we need to retrain or does Redwood handle it?
[07:22] Priya: No retraining required; we support multiple quantized execution profiles. Optimize suggests which profile for your workload based on prompt length distribution and quality thresholds. We'll surface expected regression risk per prompt set.
[07:40] Daniel: How do we verify quality parity? We want automated evals against our golden prompts and a regression alert.
[07:47] Marcus: Redwood Console has an evals harness — you can upload your golden set, run batch comparisons, and set regression thresholds that trigger alerts. We also log token-level diffs and response similarity scores.
[08:05] Tom: About rollouts — can we do canary / A/B between OpenAI and Redwood?
[08:10] Evelyn: Yes. You can split traffic by route or user cohort in the console, do A/B, compare metrics, and automatically rollback on quality regressions.
[08:21] Daniel: For the sandbox, what sample workload should we give you?
[08:25] Asha: We'll pick 50 representative prompts including system templates, short assistant responses, and three long-run conversations.
[08:31] Marcus: Perfect. We'll provision two model variants: high-precision and quantized, plus tracing hooks to show latency and token counts.
[08:40] [10:00 jump forward — demo continues with examples and occasional background noise]
[10:02] Marcus: Here's a transcript comparison — OpenAI response vs Redwood response. Note the Redwood output has slightly different punctuation and ordering sometimes. We'll run an ngram similarity and show scores in the parity sheet.
[12:15] Daniel: Are there any changes to error codes we should handle?
[12:20] Marcus: We map common error classes but codes differ. We'll provide a compatibility layer in the SDK so you can translate, but it's easiest to handle broad classes: rate_limit, invalid_request, auth_error, server_error.
[13:05] Lina: For auditability — are request/response bodies stored? For compliance we need redaction and TTL.
[13:12] Priya: You can configure redaction rules in the console and set TTLs; for Private you can disable logging entirely or forward logs to your SIEM.
[13:25] Tom: What about throughput — can you support our 200 rps burst at p95 under 500ms?
[13:32] Marcus: With Dedicated pools yes, and with right model size/quantization and batching strategy you can reach that. For hosted, p95 may vary a bit — we'll simulate your pattern in the sandbox.
[14:00] [15:10] Asha: Any gotchas with Together models? We have a custom Together variant with a tweak to sampling params.
[15:16] Marcus: Together variants sometimes expose nonstandard params; those map to Redwood model config but if you used a proprietary sampling hook we'll need to emulate it in a small shim. Usually a few lines of adapter code.
[15:35] Daniel: OK. Security follow-up: Lina will send a scoping list.
[15:40] Lina: I'll send SOC2 questions, KMS questions, and network topology checklist.
[15:45] Evelyn: We'll attach our SOC2 report and the KMS integration guide after the call.
[15:50] [20:00 summary jump] Evelyn: Quick recap — Redwood can map OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls to our chat endpoints; streaming and function-calling supported; tokenization small deltas; cost wins via quantization & batch; Private deployment supports KMS, SSO, RBAC, and retention controls.
[16:10] Daniel: Good. I want to validate quality on the golden set, the cost model, and a Private deep dive.
[16:18] Evelyn: Next steps captured: parity spreadsheet, sandbox keys, and security doc share.
[16:25] Tom: We'll aim to run sandbox tests next week.
[16:29] Asha: One more question — are there SDKs for Node/Python and prebuilt Docker runners?
[16:34] Marcus: Yes Node/Python SDKs and a docker runner for on-prem. We'll include example Helm charts for Private.
[16:42] [55:00] Evelyn: Any final Qs?
[55:07] Daniel: None from me — thanks everyone.
[55:10] Asha: Thanks.
[55:12] Lina: Thanks, talk soon.
[57:30] Evelyn: We'll follow up with the sheet and the sandbox invite.
[57:38] [end call]
